To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

energy productivity change can be decomposed into several components: changes in the ratio of non energy inputs and energy, changes in energy supply composition and output composition; technological change and technical efficiency change; that in the OECD countries between 80 and 90, technological change is the main source, increase in capital energy ration and growing importance within total supply of electricity also play an important role.
technological change and increase in capital energy ratios were the most important sources of energy productivity change in the 23 OECD countries in the 1980s.
energy productivity change in OECD countries during the 1980s is largely due to technical efficiency change and technological change, with the latter being the most important factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the decomposition of energy productivity change into its components.
the decomposition of energy productivity change into its sources and the analysis of the sources of change in energy productivity in OECD countries.
the decomposition of the total factor productivity change into several factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
technological change and the changes in the composition of energy and output are the most important determinants of energy productivity change.
technological change has been the major factor behind the energy productivity change.
energy productivity change is driven by technological change and the changes in input-output structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy efficiency improvement is mainly due to technological change and the changes in the energy supply composition.
the technological change is the major driving force for improving energy productivity, but other factors also play a significant role in energy productivity improvement. (c) 2005 Elsevier Inc. All
the main reason for the increase in energy productivity during the 1980s was technological change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decomposition approach provides useful information to energy policy makers.
energy productivity change is not only a matter of energy saving, but also the result of the changes in energy supply composition, non-energy input ratios, and output composition.

energy efficiency improvement should be considered in the context of the overall efficiency of the economy and that it is necessary to consider the composition of energy supply and demand when analyzing the energy efficiency of a country.
